title: get_in() raises TypeError when a path goes through a non-container
body:
`get_in` in `toolz/dicttoolz.py` returns `default` when the path
cannot be followed, but a path that runs into a value that cannot be
indexed with that key raises instead:

```python
>>> get_in(["a", "b"], {"a": 1})
TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable    # expected None
>>> get_in(["items", "first"], {"items": [1, 2]}, default=0)
TypeError: list indices must be integers ...      # expected 0
```

Expected: any such lookup returns `default` (None unless given), and
with `no_default=True` the original exception is raised as before.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: TypeError is no longer treated as a missing path.
